AI hasn't taken your job yet because the version required isn't available yet. But what's coming soon is the version that can out think you, and the humanoid form with dexterity on par with you. When that level of competency is uploaded to humanoid form, you'll start to realize what's happening. My hope, albeit perhaps naive, is that this will do what Elon has claimed, which is that work will become optional. I don't want to stop working, and I don't want stuff to stop being made. But humans don't need to make stuff. Robots can do that. They can consistently, 24/7, clean cities, bathrooms, grow, harvest, manufacture, package, ship, and serve coffee, and they can handle the waste management of the entire cycle at every step in this chain. This applies to every form of product and/or service. Humans can do higher brow work. But they can also opt out of work. I don't think this will create nations of do nothings. What most are not understanding is the system we live in. We mostly just make stuff, whether intellectual or physical. But we are broke. We don't have time to relax and spend time with our children and friends. Hobbies seem exhausting after 50 hours making the stuff. This can be a world that helps all of us. We just need to use it right.

Keep in mind, when you come onto a project that other developers have been working on... they already generated the code you're going to be altering, tweaking, testing, or adding to. They just did what GPT-3 does, but way more advanced and with way more specificity. GPT-3 is more like using a power drill to help you put in some screws. At some point, you're going to need to put in a nail and GPT-3 is going to want to use screws. That is when you will be needed, to overrule it and use nails. At some point in the future, it might learn to be a power drill and a nail gun... but then you'll need to use some wood glue, and it won't use wood glue. You may use GPT-3 to get an advanced skeleton, but at the end of the day someone still needs to do the rest of it. We have pretty standard ways of starting code, this will just help with starting that code with a little meat on the bones.
